target.title: fix: CLI-backend agent runtimes skip the BOOTSTRAP.md first-run ritual
target.body:
Closes #100559

> 🤖 **AI-assisted PR** (Claude Opus). Investigation, refactor, and tests were AI-assisted; changes were reviewed and validated locally on Node 24.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents on CLI-backend runtimes (`claude-cli`, `gemini-cli`) skip the `BOOTSTRAP.md` first-run ritual. On a brand-new workspace with a pending `BOOTSTRAP.md`, a CLI-backend agent replies with a generic greeting ("Hello, how can I help?") instead of running the first-run bootstrap ritual, because `BOOTSTRAP.md` reaches it only as passive Project Context, never as the blocking "Bootstrap Pending" directive. The embedded runtime (including Codex) already gates the first reply correctly; only the CLI-backend runtimes are affected. Any downstream capability gated on bootstrap completion (identity/memory setup, skill activation keyed on `BOOTSTRAP.md` deletion) stays locked indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `bootstrapMode` was computed and threaded into the system prompt only on the embedded-runner path, never on the CLI-backend path. The rendering helper `buildAgentBootstrapSystemContext` returns nothing when `bootstrapMode` is `none`/undefined, so the gate was simply absent from CLI-backend system prompts.

Rather than duplicate the routing logic, this promotes the embedded runner's bootstrap routing into a shared module `src/agents/bootstrap-routing.ts` (`resolveWorkspaceBootstrapRouting` + `isPrimaryBootstrapRun`) so both runtimes share one routing path. The CLI `prepare` step then computes `bootstrapMode` from the already-resolved bootstrap files — mirroring the embedded runner's inputs exactly (pending state, primary-run check, canonical-workspace check, and `hasBootstrapFileAccess = !disableTools`, since CLI backends are `nativeToolMode: "always-on"`) — and threads it through `buildCliAgentSystemPrompt`. The embedded-runner change is import-only (no behavior change).

Non-goal: this does **not** port the embedded runner's continuation-skip perf optimization (`hasCompletedBootstrapTurn`). It is unnecessary for the gate — `isWorkspaceBootstrapPending` returns `false` once `BOOTSTRAP.md` is deleted, so the gate naturally disappears after bootstrap completes. Codex is unaffected: it runs on the embedded runtime and already renders the gate.

## User Impact

Agents on CLI-backend runtimes (`claude-cli`, `gemini-cli`) now run the `BOOTSTRAP.md` first-run ritual on a bootstrap-pending workspace, matching the embedded runtime. First-run onboarding and any capability gated on bootstrap completion now work on the CLI backends. No config or API changes; no impact on already-bootstrapped workspaces (the gate only renders while `BOOTSTRAP.md` is pending).

## Evidence

**Original defect (empirical):** on an identical fresh workspace with a pending `BOOTSTRAP.md`, an embedded-runtime agent (`openai`/Codex, GPT-5.5) enters bootstrap on a `Hello` first message, while a `claude-cli`/Opus agent does not — it greets instead. This PR makes the CLI path render the same "Bootstrap Pending" gate.

**Local validation (Node 24.18.0, pnpm 11.2.2):**
- `pnpm build` ✅ (no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `check:cli-bootstrap-imports` / `check:plugin-sdk-exports` pass)
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` (typecheck) ✅
- `pnpm lint` (oxlint) ✅
- `pnpm check:import-cycles` ✅ (0 runtime value cycles — the new shared module introduces none)
- `codex review --uncommitted` ✅ (no correctness issues)
- Focused tests ✅:
  - `src/agents/bootstrap-routing.test.ts` (moved from the embedded runner; adds `isPrimaryBootstrapRun` coverage)
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.system-prompt.test.ts` (new cases: `full` renders the gate + "included below in Project Context" wording; `limited` renders limited guidance; no `bootstrapMode` omits the gate)
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.bootstrap-context.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`, `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`

New tests assert the exact gate wording now emitted on the CLI path (`## Bootstrap Pending`, "follow it before replying normally", "must follow BOOTSTRAP.md, not a generic greeting").
